text:
Sofia Ivanova: heads up, I think we have a deterministic-ish deadlock path when a streaming request disconnects mid-step in TP. Seeing TP group go "no forward progress" until watchdog kills the whole worker. This looks like the cancel path causes one rank to skip a barrier that other ranks still hit.

Marcus Reed: yep, I can repro in staging with forced client cancel. Pattern: one rank returns early from decode loop, others sit in `tp_barrier(step_end)` waiting. After that, scheduler keeps that group "busy" forever.

Julian Moore: do we have logs showing which barrier? is it the scheduler barrier or the kernel-side collective fence?

Marcus Reed: scheduler barrier. Here’s the relevant snippet from `runtime-worker` logs (4-way TP, A100):
```
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] decode_step=214 begin
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] stream_write failed: client_disconnect
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] cancel requested; reason=STREAM_BROKEN
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] cancel: marking req canceled and returning from step loop
[tp=0 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] decode_step=214 end -> barrier(wait)
[tp=1 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] decode_step=214 end -> barrier(wait)
[tp=2 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] decode_step=214 end -> barrier(wait)
[tp=0 group=tpgrp-17] barrier(wait) stalled > 60s (pending=1)
```
Rank 3 never enters barrier.

Sofia Ivanova: that matches my suspicion. Current flow is roughly:
- per-step: enqueue compute + NCCL, then `scheduler_barrier(step_end)` to keep ranks aligned
- cancel path can short-circuit out of the loop before the step_end barrier
So other ranks block indefinitely.

Samir Qureshi: is the barrier keyed by request id or TP group state? like, does it wait for "all active ranks" or just "all ranks"?

Sofia Ivanova: today it’s "all ranks in group", no notion of per-rank cancellation completion. It’s basically a group rendezvous.

Hiro Tanaka: question: why do we even need step_end barrier for decode? (I know it was to avoid rank drift for KV cache). If a rank exits early, the KV cache state is already inconsistent anyway.

Marcus Reed: we do it to keep scheduler accounting sane + avoid rank getting ahead and enqueueing next token while others still running prior token. But for cancel specifically, we should have a coordinated abort.

Grace Kim: do we know if rank 3 is actually exiting the whole request, or just the streaming writer? In some code paths we "detach" the stream but keep generating for logging.

Marcus Reed: in this repro, it fully cancels. I forced it via `--cancel_after_tokens=200` in the test harness (close TCP). Rank 3 sees broken pipe and sets cancel.

Julian Moore: can we confirm the cancel signal is per-rank (local) not broadcast? That seems like the core issue: one rank decides to bail, others keep going.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. Cancel currently comes from the HTTP worker on the same host -> only affects the rank handling the stream write. The other ranks don’t know until they hit something that checks shared request state (which they won’t, because they’re blocked in barrier).

Omar El-Sayed: I looked at traces for one of the prod hangs last week, and the spans end exactly at `tp_group_barrier_wait`. No downstream NCCL errors, just waiting. So this aligns.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE side, this is the kind of hang where watchdog/quarantine will help, but we still need correctness here. Otherwise we’ll quarantine a lot on noisy clients.

Sofia Ivanova: agreed. Proposed fix direction:
1) make cancellation "collective" at TP group level: if any rank cancels a request, all ranks must observe it and enter a coordinated abort path
2) barriers must be cancellation-safe: if request is canceled, barrier should release everyone (or convert to abort barrier)

Hiro Tanaka: there’s another twist: we also have CUDA stream/event fences around collectives. If rank 3 returns early and destroys per-request CUDA events, others might wait on an event that never signals. But your logs show it’s stuck in scheduler barrier first.

Grace Kim: but even if we fix scheduler barrier, we need to ensure we don’t leave in-flight NCCL ops orphaned. If one rank tears down communicators while others still executing, we’ll get undefined behavior / async errors later.

Sofia Ivanova: yep. But step 1 is to not deadlock.

Marcus Reed: I did a quick local patch: instead of `return` on cancel, I force a `goto step_end_barrier` so every rank always hits barrier, then exits. That fixes repro, BUT it still hangs if cancel happens *before* compute is enqueued on one rank (rare, but can happen with timeout cancel). Then barrier happens but other ranks have enqueued compute+NCCL and wait on completion; canceled rank skips and later steps still weird.

Julian Moore: can you share the specific code path? is it `RequestContext::maybe_cancel()` inside `decode_loop()`?

Marcus Reed: roughly:
```
while (tokens < max) {
  if (req->is_canceled()) return Status::Canceled;
  run_decode_step(req);
  tp_group_barrier(req->id, step);
}
```
`run_decode_step` enqueues compute and returns immediately (async), then barrier is what keeps ranks aligned.

Sofia Ivanova: yep, this is brittle. Better pattern:
- always execute a "step" state machine on all ranks
- cancellation is just a flag that affects what we enqueue (maybe enqueue a no-op / dummy allreduce) but we still rendezvous

Samir Qureshi: simplest: introduce `tp_group_abort_barrier(req_id, step, abort_reason)` that:
- if any rank enters with abort_reason != none, it marks group/request as aborting
- all ranks entering barrier get released once all ranks have entered OR once timeout triggers and we force abort

Grace Kim: careful with timeout: if one rank never enters because it’s truly dead, you still need the watchdog to tear down. But for disconnect cancel, it should converge.

Omar El-Sayed: can we add a metric here? `tp_barrier_wait_ms{reason=step_end, canceled=true/false}` and log the per-rank state when barrier wait exceeds N ms.

Julian Moore: +1, and include `rank_seen_cancel` boolean in the structured log so we can confirm broadcast is working.

Isabella Rossi: I can run microbench on barrier changes, but note: if we add a bunch of atomic checks in the hot loop it might regress token latency.

Sofia Ivanova: ideally cancellation checks are not every iteration for normal case. But cancel is relatively rare; we can do the broadcast only on cancel.

Hiro Tanaka: how to broadcast? options:
- use shared host memory (since ranks are processes) + periodic polling
- use NCCL to signal cancel (but that itself can hang)
- use scheduler control plane to notify all ranks

Marcus Reed: since this is intra-host TP group, we already have shared-memory control for scheduler tokens. We can extend the existing `GroupMailbox` to send `CANCEL(req_id)` to all ranks.

Sofia Ivanova: yes. Concrete proposal:
- when a rank decides request is canceled (client disconnect, timeout), it sends `CancelRequest(req_id, reason)` to group mailbox
- all ranks check mailbox at safe points (start/end of step) and set `req->cancelled=true`
- step_end barrier becomes:
  - always entered by all ranks while req is "active" OR "aborting"
  - if aborted, we still execute a minimal step_end: flush outstanding work bookkeeping, do not enqueue next step

Grace Kim: what about the case where one rank is blocked inside NCCL and never hits mailbox check? then others will reach barrier and still hang.

Hiro Tanaka: that’s separate (collective stall). But for this specific thread, the issue is skipping barrier due to early return, not NCCL stall.

Rafael Mendes: from incidents, we see both. But fixing this one should reduce frequency. Also: if we quarantine TP group after hang, we don’t want cancel/disconnect to trigger quarantine constantly.

Sofia Ivanova: right. We should treat cancel-induced abort as "expected" and not count it as group fault.

Julian Moore: can we add log lines to confirm? e.g.
`tp_group_barrier_release reason=cancel req=... ranks_in=4/4`.

Marcus Reed: I can do that.

Sofia Ivanova: also please check another edge case: multi-request batch. If we batch multiple reqs in same step, cancel of one req should not force others to abort. The barrier is per-step, not per-request.

Marcus Reed: good catch. In the repro, it’s single request per group due to long seq. But in prod we batch. The barrier should not be per-request; it’s per "microbatch step".

Hiro Tanaka: exactly. If barrier is per-step, cancellation must not allow one rank to exit the step early while others are still executing the step for other requests.

Sofia Ivanova: so maybe the correct abstraction is:
- ranks execute `Step(step_id, batch_id)`
- cancellation marks a request as "inactive" for future steps, but does NOT short-circuit current step
- streaming disconnect should only stop IO; compute continues until next safe point? That has cost implications.

Grace Kim: cost vs correctness: If client disconnects, continuing compute for that request is wasted. But if cancel mid-step causes deadlock, we need a safe cutoff.

Marcus Reed: alternative: on disconnect, mark request canceled, but let current step finish on all ranks (since compute already enqueued). Then it will be removed before next step. That seems reasonable.

Sofia Ivanova: yes. Implement as: don’t `return` immediately. Instead set cancel flag, and the loop will not schedule new steps after finishing the current step + barrier.

Julian Moore: + ensure `run_decode_step` doesn’t get called again if canceled.

Marcus Reed: I think we already have that check at loop top, but it’s the immediate return that breaks barrier.

Omar El-Sayed: can someone paste the exact function name so I can search logs? I want to add a span around it for the triage playbook.

Marcus Reed: `Scheduler::run_decode_loop()` calls `DecodeExecutor::step()` then `TpGroup::barrier()`.

Sofia Ivanova: action items:
- Marcus: patch cancel path to become "defer cancel until safe point" (finish step -> hit barrier -> exit), and add mailbox broadcast if needed
- Julian/Omar: add structured logging around barrier wait and cancel state
- Grace/Hiro: sanity-check interaction with in-flight collectives (do we need to call `ncclCommAbort` on cancel? I think no for this case)

Hiro Tanaka: I’d vote no abort on cancel; only abort for comm errors / watchdog. Cancel should be graceful.

Grace Kim: agree. Aborting NCCL on cancel is a hammer.

Marcus Reed: quick patch diff (pseudo) for discussion:
```
// before
if (req->is_canceled()) return Canceled;

// after
if (req->is_canceled()) {
  req->set_cancel_deferred(true);
}
run_decode_step(req);
barrier(step);
if (req->cancel_deferred()) return Canceled;
```
But need to ensure `run_decode_step` becomes a no-op if cancel happens before enqueue.

Sofia Ivanova: yes, in that case:
- if cancel_deferred is set *before* enqueue, we should not enqueue compute; but still must barrier. So:
```
if (!req->cancel_deferred()) run_decode_step(req);
barrier(step);
if (req->cancel_deferred()) return Canceled;
```

Marcus Reed: good. I’ll implement and rerun repro.

Isabella Rossi: if you add a branch in the hot path, can you also add a counter of how often it triggers? so we can estimate impact.

Marcus Reed: yep.

--- later ---

Marcus Reed: update: patch fixes the repro hang in 50/50 runs.
Command:
`tp_stress --tp=4 --concurrency=32 --streaming --cancel_after_tokens=200 --seq_len_mix=long`
Before: hang within ~3-7 min. After: no hangs in 40 min.

Marcus Reed: logs now show:
```
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] stream_write failed: client_disconnect
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] cancel requested; deferring to step boundary
[tp=0 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] step_end barrier enter (cancel_seen=false)
[tp=1 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] step_end barrier enter (cancel_seen=false)
[tp=2 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] step_end barrier enter (cancel_seen=false)
[tp=3 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] step_end barrier enter (cancel_seen=true)
[tp=0 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] step_end barrier release (4/4)
[tp=0 group=tpgrp-17 req=6f2a] exiting decode loop: canceled_at_step_boundary
```
Other ranks don’t log cancel_seen because they didn’t get mailbox broadcast yet (they only check local req flag). But they still exit cleanly because after barrier the scheduler observes request removed.

Julian Moore: nice. But we should make cancel_seen consistent across ranks for debugging. Otherwise we’ll still have confusion in triage.

Sofia Ivanova: agreed, but as long as they don’t deadlock it’s acceptable for patch. Let’s still add a small group-level broadcast as follow-up if it’s easy.

Omar El-Sayed: re: logs/metrics, I can add:
- `tp_barrier_wait_ms` histogram
- `tp_barrier_stall_total` counter (when > threshold)
- structured log when wait > 5s including `pending_ranks`

Rafael Mendes: please include the threshold in config so oncall can tune without rebuild.

Sofia Ivanova: +1.

Grace Kim: any test coverage? we should add a regression test that simulates cancel mid-stream and asserts barrier completes.

Marcus Reed: I can add a deterministic unit/integration test in the TP stress runner: inject cancel at token N on a single rank and assert group doesn’t hang.

Hiro Tanaka: watch out: "cancel on single rank" is the whole problem. But yes, that’s the right regression.

Sofia Ivanova: ok, let’s do this:
- ship minimal cancel-at-step-boundary fix + regression test
- follow-up: group mailbox cancel broadcast + better per-rank cancel visibility
I’ll also drop a note in the design doc that this closes the specific barrier deadlock class.

Marcus Reed: I’ll open PR today and link here.

Julian Moore: :thumbsup: ping me for review on scheduler bits.

Omar El-Sayed: ping me for logging/metrics review.

Rafael Mendes: once PR is up, I’ll sanity-check against incident patterns + what we want in the runbook.

Sofia Ivanova: thanks all. This should take a chunk out of the "hang after disconnect" tickets.
